question: A, B and C can do a piece of work in 2, 20 and 20 days respectively. How long (in days) will they take to do thrice the same work, working together?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let total work be the LCM of 2, 20, and 20, which is 20 units.

Combined efficiency of A, B, and C = (20 ÷ 2) + (20 ÷ 20) + (20 ÷ 20) = 10 + 1 + 1 = 12 units/day.

Thrice the total work = 3 × 20 = 60 units.

Time taken by them together = 60 ÷ 12 = 5 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by A = 2 days

Time taken by B = 20 days

Time taken by C = 20 days

**Calculations:**

⇒ Combined Efficiency of A, B, and C = 10 + 1 + 1 = 12 units/day

⇒ Target Work = 3 × Total Work

⇒ Target Work = 3 × 20 = 60 units

⇒ Time taken to complete target work = Target Work ÷ Combined Efficiency

⇒ Time taken = 60 ÷ 12 = 5 days

**∴ The correct answer is 5 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes & Cisterns

This concept follows the same rules as Time & Work. The key difference is that filling pipes have a positive efficiency while emptying pipes (leaks) have a negative efficiency.

Work & Wages

Total wages are always distributed among workers in the ratio of the total work done by them. If all persons work for the same number of days, wages are distributed in the direct ratio of their efficiencies.

Alternate Day Work

When individuals work on alternate days, calculate the total work completed in a single cycle (e.g., a 2-day or 3-day cycle) and then multiply it by an integer to get close to the total work.
